title: Zero total influence implies constancy
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$. If the total influence of the real-valued version of $f$ is zero, then $f$ takes the same value at every pair of inputs; in particular, $f$ is constant.
hypotheses_covered: The total influence of its real-valued version is zero
